newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BSE suspends trading in Cofinec.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BSE suspends trading in Cofinec.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange suspended trading in the Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) of packaging firm Cofinec for the day following an initial surge in its price on Tuesday, traders said.
"It was suspended for today," a floor trader told Reuters over the phone. The stock exchange was not available for immediate comment.
Cofinec GDRs opened at 4,060 forints, below Monday's close at 4,065 forints, and after they soared to 5,460 forints by 1135 GMT.
An analyst, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the possible reason behind the GDR's surge was that Cofinec officials invited a group of analysts to visit their plants in Poland and Hungary.
"I can easily see a link between the price rise and the analysts' visit," the analyst said.
A Cofinec official confirmed to Reuters that the company invited analysts for a two-day visit starting today in Cofinec's Polish unit and continuing on Wednesday in Hungary.
